instructions:
Read the paper below and produce a structured summary.

It matched these tracked topics; `relevance` must contain one entry per slug, stating what this paper changes for that topic:
- overthinking: Overthinking — When and why large reasoning models think more than a problem needs (or less than it needs) — the accuracy/efficiency tradeoff of reasoning length, test-time compute scaling, and methods to make a model stop, or keep going, at the right point.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

concepts: string - reusable ideas this paper relies on or introduces
datasets: string - datasets, benchmarks, corpora or simulators used
output_schema.limitations: string - stated limits plus any the reader should notice
output_schema.method: string - how it works, enough for a reader to explain it
methods: string - named methods, architectures or algorithms
output_schema.one_liner: string - what the paper does, in one sentence, no hype
output_schema.problem: string - the problem it addresses and why it is open

relevance.<topic-slug>: string - why this matters for that specific topic

output_schema.results: string - headline numbers, on which benchmarks, against what

payload.title: SpecExit: Accelerating Large Reasoning Model via Speculative Exit

contributions: Proposes SpecExit, an early-exit framework for large reasoning models that uses a lightweight draft model to jointly predict upcoming tokens and an early-exit signal in a single step, avoiding the extra probing overhead of prior early-exit methods
Shows internal model representations (already used in speculative decoding) also carry information about when reasoning has effectively finished
Reports up to 66% reduction in generation length and 2.5x end-to-end speedup while preserving accuracy
result.limitations: No PDF was attached; the abstract does not specify benchmark names, model sizes, or accuracy numbers beyond the headline length-reduction and speedup figures, so those details could not be extracted.
result.method: A lightweight draft model, run alongside the target large reasoning model in a manner similar to speculative decoding, simultaneously forecasts the next tokens and an early-exit signal from internal representations; when the signal indicates reasoning is complete, generation is halted without a separate probing pass, cutting output length while aiming to preserve answer accuracy.
result.one_liner: Uses a speculative-decoding-style draft model to predict both next tokens and an early-exit signal, letting a large reasoning model stop generating once its own internal representations indicate reasoning is done.
result.problem: Large reasoning models generate excessively long chains of thought, and prior early-exit mechanisms that try to shorten this reduce length but add detection overhead that limits speedup and adapts poorly across problems.

relevance.overthinking: This is a direct, substantive contribution to the topic: it is a method for making a reasoning model stop at the right point, targeting exactly the overthinking problem of unnecessarily long generation, with reported reductions of up to 66% in generation length and a 2.5x end-to-end speedup while preserving accuracy.

result.results: Up to 66% generation length reduction and 2.5x end-to-end speedup reported, with accuracy stated as preserved; specific benchmark names and per-task accuracy numbers were not available in the accessible source material.
